lines.text: Shalom alechim, it's Zayn Cheshvin, the Rebbe, fabreng many times, spoke about the importance of Abish Yisroh,
the fact that we don't ask for rain at Yisroh until today, because this was the most amount of time that it took someone to walk back from Yerushalayim,
from making the pilgrimage to Healer Egel, to his house, wherever it was.
But on this day, my wife had a miracle, and there's a story with the Rebbe, and I want to share it with people.
I think it will be inspirational, and it can be used.
Basically, it was 1985, I believe November of 1985, and my wife was pregnant with our oldest child, our only son,
Acha Mendel, maybe well, he lives in Florida today, and she went to a birthing class.
At that night, it was Sunday night, 1985, it was the last night, the night of Zayn Cheshvin.
It was Sunday night, so the Rebbe was fabrengen, so I asked my wife if usually I would take her,
go with her to the class, and wait for her outside and all that, there was a birthing class,
and all that. So this time, I said, do you mind if you drive yourself?
So I could listen to fabrengen, so she said sure.
And the fabrengen ended, remember, we're in California, on Schliches, Marin County,
so it's three hours, three hours, New York is three hours ahead of California.
So when the Rebbe finished fabrengen, about 12 o'clock or so, or 12.30, I think it was 12.30 more,
it was already 9.30 at night. So I figured that the class is, I think it was 7.30 or 8,
and by 9.30 she was usually home. Anyway, she wasn't home, it was 12.30 California time,
fabrengen finished already, and I'm waiting, give it a half hour, she's still not home.
I get worried, I call a few of my balabatim, and they say wait longer, give it some more time,
an hour passes by, and she's not home, and I get very worried.
All of a sudden the door opens up, and my wife walks through the door with a policeman,
a tall sheriff behind her, and he says, Rabbi, you have what to be thankful to God for.
And he tells me the story that she was driving back on the 101 freeway, a four-lane highway,
in the further lane number one, and a drunk driver speeding at 90 miles an hour,
being chased by the police, went right into our brand new Toyota Corolla that we bought,
and it was totaled, she opened her seatbelt, she put on her wig which fell off,
and here she is, a miracle. Naturally, I was very shook up,
and I asked Rabbi Reitschik, or Maspia, I asked Rabbi Reitschik,
I asked him, what's the lesson here, you know, she's a good person, there's obviously lessons,
he said, I don't know, write to the Rabbi.
I wrote to the Rabbi, and the Rabbi sent back a letter first wishing her to have an easy
pregnancy and delivery, and the baby should be well, and then there was the P.S.
Then the P.S. was, the lesson from the episode that you wrote to me about,
Goedl injen hazrizus bechol injoni toyef, the greatness of alacrity, of zrizus,
of swiftness, shnelkite, in all matters of goodness, not just Toyota or Mitsus.
Whenever it comes to something good, do it with great zrizus, great alacrity,
great zest and don't procrastinate.
This Terebus said is the lesson, he didn't say how he came to determine that this is the lesson,
but I assume, because I wrote to him the details, I remember vividly writing to him that the drive was driving so fast,
everything I said to you. Years later, I realized that in the moment that Terebus said that night,
the P.S. was a Pajas lechlicho, the Terebus spoke about the Avrom Babuika,
which is the idea of Avrom got up very early to bring Yitzchok as a carbon, the Akeda,
and he didn't procrastinate, but he did it, he rose early in the morning to do it,
because he was going to do a mitzvah for Hashem.
And if you learn the Maimer really, it doesn't seem that that part of the Maimer
is really relevant to the rest of the Maimer, at least outwardly it looks that way.
Bottom line is, Terebus said it.
I realized that what Terebus said in the Maimer by Hashem Avrom Babuika was the idea of srisus,
the Kdusha of holiness, which was the prelude for the srisus, the clip,
the hate of the negative type of quickness of the accident.
So Terebus in his Maimer, which he said in New York, before the accident happened,
he didn't send it for the healing before the maca,
because Tzadikim adayim levayim, Tzadikim are similar to Dakotash Borchul, et cetera, et cetera,
but Meila, just as the Abish, just as God does so, so do Tzadikim do.
We should in Skoyom Meila and Skoyom Nasim these days are remembered,
and we need to make, how do we remember them by Nasim, by implementing them,
maybe so in everyone's life, to implement and to know that the Rebbe,
our Rebbe loves us and he thinks about us, and we just need to get out of the way
and do what he wants, and everything will be fine and dandy.
Lechayim lechayim lechayim levrochem masiach now.
